title: Disruption
body:
Disruption will assist payers in assessing the competitiveness of their network to another network using utilization data provided by an employer looking to switch health plans. ## Accessing Disruption
The Disruption module requires activation by Zelis, on the client, project and user levels. Once this has been completed, Disruption is accessible under **Sales Tools** in the left column navigation. Depending on your setup, you may see **Disruption (new version)**, **Disruption (old version)** or both. This help content is for **Disruption (new version)**. There are two versions of the Disruption Landing Page. We will refer to them as the **getting started** page and the **Analysis List** page. When you access Disruption for the first time (never uploaded a Utilization File), the **getting started** page will be displayed (shown in the screenshot below). There are three boxes in the center of the **getting started** page. They are: * Import Utilization File * Create/View Matching Configurations * Create Disruption Analysis Here you can begin by Importing a Utilization File. Each box will be checked off as you move through the process of creating an analysis. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/disruption_gettingstarted_1.png) Once you have created an analysis, or an analysis has been shared, you will no longer see the **getting started** page. Instead, you will be brought to the **Analysis List** view (shown in the screenshot below), where the Utilization Files, Matching Configurations, and Create Analysis buttons will be available. Manage Disruption Analyses page displays **My Analyses** option in **Viewing** by default. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/disruption-manage-disruption-analysis-my-analysis.png) If you have not created any analyses, select the **All Analyses** option to view shared analyses. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/disruption-manage-disruption-analysis-all-analysis.png) You can view an existing analysis by clicking on the **Analysis Name** or clicking on **View** option in Ellipse menu or search the required analysis by typing the Analysis Name in search bar. Utilization file validation prevents empty or invalid uploads. ## Running a Disruption Analysis To perform a Disruption analysis, you will need the following: * Utilization File \ Uploaded by clients into the Disruption module; it contains data on claims aggregated at the provider, address, and TIN levels. * Mapping of the utilization file headers to the Zelis standard column names \ Clients will also map the columns that are in the Utilization File to the standard columns of data available in Network360 * Matching configuration \ This is created within the Disruption module of Network360. A Matching Configuration allows you to define the parameters checked during the analysis portion of this process.

Importing a Utilization File
To import a Utilization file: 1. Navigate to **Disruption**, then click on **Utilization Files.** 2. Click on **+ Import File.** 3. Navigate to the file location to drag and drop the file onto the Upload section OR Click the **Upload** section to select the file, then click the Open button. **Note:** The maximum file size is 100 mb; the recommended format is .csv, but xlsx and xls are also supported formats. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/importingutilizationfile.png) Below the Upload section, are fields to enter the following information about the file: * **Name**: Enter a name for the file. The name is required to be unique within the Disruption module. The name will be referenced throughout the module. For example, the name will be listed in the Dashboard and available in a dropdown list when setting up Matching Configurations. * **Description**: This is an optional field where you can enter a brief description of the file. * **Delimiter**: This is an optional field where you can select the appropriate delimiter for the data within the .csv file. (If an Excel file is uploaded, this field does not apply). * **Expiration**: Expiration options available: 60 days, 90 days, or Never Expire. The Default option is 60 days from the date of importing. * **Sharing**: If the Sharing checkbox is not selected, the file will be private, which means that only you will be able to view/use the file. If the Sharing checkbox is selected, all users of the Disruption module within your organization will be able to use the file. **Note**: Admin users will be able to view all Utilization Files by selecting the option to view shared files. This includes private and shared files. * Click the **Save** button. When a Utilization File is uploaded it goes through a validation process. During this process, you will see the **Processing Files** page displayed. The **Status** of your uploaded file will change from **Validating** to **Mapping**. When the status is Mapping, you can map the file by clicking on the ellipse's menu (in the last column) and selecting **Map**. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/mapping_map.png "ProcessingFilesPage") ### Editing Utilization Files You can edit a Utilization file via the Edit option from ellipses menu from either the Utilization Files page or Processing Files page. The elements that can be edited are: Name, Description, Delimiter, Expiration Date, and to Share or Not Share the file. You can also access the Quality Score and Standard Mapped Columns from the Edit page by clicking on the associated View link. Export options include: Standardized Original File and QA Output File. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/disruption_v2_filedetailspage.png) **Notes:** * Options in the ellipse's menu will change based on the status of the file, except for **View** and **Delete** - these options are constants. * If the status is **Running** (shaded in blue), **Cancel** will be an option in the ellipsis menu. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/running_cancel.png "ProcessingFilesPageCancel") * If the status is x **Cancelled**, **Rerun** will be an option. * If a running job is cancelled during Computing Quality Score, the **Rerun** option will be available in the menu. When Rerun is clicked, the analysis will rerun from the point of cancellation. **Note:** When Cancel is clicked, the status will change to **ANALYSIS CANCELLED**. It may take some time for the status to change. In the background there are 8 steps to analysis. If the system is in the middle of one of those steps, it will wait until the step is completed before changing the status. By default, the Disruption page is refreshed every 10 seconds. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/cancel_rerun.png "ProcessingFilesPageRerun")

Column Aliases
You can find Zelis Standard Columns by navigating to **Utilization Files > File Details > Mapped Columns** page. For each Zelis Standard Column, you can create one or more Column Aliases that correspond to column headers commonly used in your Utilization Files. Column Aliases that match a header in a new Utilization File will be automatically mapped to a Zelis Standard Column, eliminating the need to manually map these columns for each new import. **Note**: If a column name on the Utilization File already matches a Zelis Standard Column Name, it will automatically be mapped. ### Adding Column Aliases To add column Aliases, click on **Column Aliases** on the **Utilization Files** page. Select a **Zelis Standard Column** from the dropdown list, then type one or more desired aliases and click on **Save Aliases**. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/addingcolumnaliases.png "AddingColumnAliases") All added Aliases are displayed at the bottom of the page with **Edit** and **Delete** options for each. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/current-aliases.png "CurrentAliases")

Mapping Columns
The columns from the Utilization File need to be mapped to the Zelis Standard Column Names used in Network360. Mapping is necessary so that the data in the columns in the imported Utilization File can be recognized by Network360 and then validated. If a column header from a Utilization file already matches a Zelis Standard Column Name, it will map automatically. Once the uploaded Utilization File is in the Mapping status on the Processing Files page, you can map the Utilization File Column Names to the Zelis Standard Column Names used by Network360. ### Mapping Process On the **Processing Files** page, click on the Utilization File name. This will open the **File Details**. Click on the **Standard Mapped Columns - View** link. The **Mapping** list will be displayed. **Utilization File Column Name** is the name of the column taken from the Utilization File. Each **Zelis Standard Column Name** dropdown list contains the mapping options. There are two ways to start the Mapping process. Once the status says "Mapping", you can start the mapping process by: Selecting the Utilization File name > File Details > View Standard Map Columns OR Selecting the ellipses on **Processing Files** page and select **Map.** ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/mappingcolumns.png "MappingColumns") To map a column, select the toggle button to the right of the field to activate it. Then, within the **Zelis Standard Column Name** dropdown list, select the appropriate column name. The **Passthrough** option means that the original data from the Utilization File column will be passed through without being mapped to a Zelis Standard Column. The more data that is mapped, the better your analysis results will be. Therefore, it is recommended to map all columns. **Note**: When selecting “name” fields from the Zelis Standard Column Name dropdown list, either FirstName and/or LastName OR FullName can be mapped. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/mappingcolumnsdropdown.png "MappingColumnsDropdown")
Click the **Save and Continue** button at the bottom of the page to save the mappings. Once the mappings are saved, the status on the **Processing Files** page will change from Computing Quality Scores to **Review**. When the status is Review, you can review the preliminary Quality Scoring information by selecting **Review Quality Score** in the ellipse's menu. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/ellipsesreviewqualityscore.png)

Quality Scoring
Once a Utilization File has been uploaded and mapped, a review and validation for completeness and accuracy of a selection of the data is performed (the system looks at the first 300 rows – this is noted in the messaging below Quality Scoring: file name, at the top of the screen). ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/qualityscoring1.png "QualityScoring") **Quality Scoring** provides you with information about the data in the Utilization File and the ability to increase the quality of the data. Six categories of information are validated. A brief validation explanation is provided below each category heading. **General** – This validation checks for any missing fields. **NPI Data** – This validation checks to see if an NPI has been populated. **Recommended Data** – This validation checks for the presence of data elements within the Utilization File that are the most useful for analysis. The validation process checks and reports whether any of these recommended data elements are missing in your Utilization File. When an element is missing, you can correct this by adjusting the column mapping or importing another Utilization File that includes the data element(s) missing in the original file. The Recommended Data Columns are: * Address * City * FacilityName * FirstName * FullName * LastName * NPI * State * TaxID * Zip **Note:** If **FirstName** and **LastName** are mapped, then mapping **FullName** is not needed and will not be available in the drop down of Recommended Data columns. Similarly, if **FullName** is mapped, then **FirstName** and **LastName** are not available in the drop down of Recommended Data columns. **City/State Match** – This checks to ensure the City/State combination is accurate. **Zip Code Check** – This verifies that the zip codes within the Utilization File are valid. If Zip Code is 4-digit from utilization file, we add a leading 0 to make it the required 5-digit. **NPI Validation** – This validation checks for the accuracy of the provider’s NPI. If a category of data was not included in the Validation File, a **Not mapped** message is provided under the category name. To view details on the validation of a category, select the adjacent radio button. The details will be displayed below the list of categories. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/qualityscoring2.png "QualityScoring2") When you view the details of a validation category, you will see the specific data elements and whether they are included, missing or questionable in the Utilization File. Then, you can determine whether the missing or questionable elements can be mapped, or the Utilization File needs to be changed. At times it may be desired to change a Utilization File to get a better-quality score. If a change is needed, you can either upload the Utilization File with a new name or delete the current file and reupload the file using the same name. Bulk file deletion is possible in both Processing and Utilization File pages. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/disruption-processing-files-bulk-delete.png) ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/disruption-utilization-files-bulk-delete.png) Also, tooltip messages, confirmation and error messages help user to understand the status. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/disruption-tooltip-help.png) **Note**: When importing a changed file, it is necessary to give it a unique name in the Disruption module and redo the mapping. ### Approval/Rejection of Utilization File Once the quality score information has been reviewed, you can Approve or Reject the Utilization File. If you click **Approve**, the file will be imported and ready to be used. If you **Reject** a file, that imported Utilization File will be deleted and removed from the Processing Files page. A new file will need to be imported and mapped again. A confirmation message will be displayed to ensure that you want to continue to Reject a file. A timestamp of the approval or rejection is listed in the Processing Files page.

Matching Configurations

 ### Overview A Matching Configuration is a set of various combinations of parameters (known as Passes) along with selected product and network information saved as a profile (or set of rules) to qualify the data's accuracy. There are three types of passes: * Full Match: Requires an exact match between the value in the utilization file and the providers table. * Prefix Match: Matches providers whose names or addresses start with the prefix from the utilization file, allowing for partial matches. * Radius Match: Searches for providers located within a 1 to 50-mile radius of a geolocation point specified by the address, city, state in the utilization file. ### Creating a Matching Configuration Only admin users in the system can create a Matching Configuration. Non-admin users can view and use the Matching Configurations but are restricted from making changes. To create a Matching Configuration: 1. Navigate to **Disruption** 2. Click on **Matching Configurations** 3. Click on **Create New Configuration** 4. In the top left corner enter a unique **Name** for the configuration. This is required. 5. Enter a **Target Competitor** for the configuration. This is optional but it can be used to help filter the list of matching configurations. 6. Enter a **Description** for the configuration. This is optional but is a way to help identify the Matching Configuration. 7. Select a **Network Type**. This is a required field. 8. Select a **Product Type**. This is a required field. 9. Select a **Line of Business**. This is a required field. 10. **Sharing** is an optional field. If selected, the Matching Configuration can be used by others (including non-admin users) in your organization. If Sharing is not selected, the file will only be available to you and other admin users. 11. Select a **Reference Utilization File**. This allows you to select an existing Utilization File to demonstrate how well it conforms to a particular Matching Configuration. The bottom portion of the screen contains the many matching passes performed on Utilization Files, categorized by **High Confidence**, **Medium Confidence**, **Low Confidence**. * **High Confidence** matching passes use a strict criterion for various passes, all of which include TIN. * **Medium Confidence** provides some variability with some of the matching passes (for example, characters) but still utilizes a good number of standard columns to provide a decent match. * **Low Confidence** uses fewer standard columns, and possibly less characters, to match. Once a **Reference Utilization File** has been selected, the passes at the bottom of the page will update with information on which ones are valid and which ones are invalid. Each one can be expanded to view the specific element that is invalid. If you want to see only valid matching passes for this reference utilization file, you can filter the list by selecting the **Show only valid Passes** toggle button. **Note:** Selecting a Reference Utilization File is NOT necessary. It is used as a helpful guideline. 12. Select one or more **Passes** to be applied to the configuration, from any or all Confidence levels. **Note**: The fields in a pass may appear to be the same as in another pass, however, the number of characters that are being matched for a field can be different. Expand passes to view differences. 13. Click the **Save** button in the top right corner of the screen. Once saved, the Matching Configurations page will be displayed. The saved Matching Configuration can be reused each time a similarly formatted Utilization File is uploaded. A saved Matching Configuration is selected in the **Create Analysis** step. ### Matching Configurations Page The Zelis Recommended Passes is a preset list of matching passes that a user can use for their Disruption analysis. This is a standardized template that all Disruption clients will have upon implementation. Recommended Passes helps clients to use Disruption without having to setup a matching configuration. Permission-based tooltips and delete restrictions are added for **Matching Configuration** page. As an Admin user: * You can filter the list to display **All Configurations** or **My Configurations**. My Configurations will show you configurations that you did not share with others. * Selecting one of the listed Matching Configurations will open a view where a different Reference Utilization File can be selected and compared with the selected passes. * Clicking on triple dot button in the last column for an existing Matching Configuration will allow you to edit that Matching Configuration to add or remove passes and change the parameters. * The columns can also be sorted and filtered by any user.

Disruption Analysis
Use Disruption Analysis to gain valuable insight into the data from an uploaded Utilization File using a selected Matching Configuration and compare it to other networks. Once you have the specific Utilization File uploaded and a Matching Configuration (new or existing), an analysis can be run. 1. Select the **Create Analysis** button to get started. The Create Analysis page will display. 2. Fill in the appropriate fields. **Analysis Name**: This is a required field. The name of the analysis needs to be unique in the system. If you enter a name that is not unique, an error message will display. **Description**: This is an optional field where you can enter a brief description of the analysis. **Utilization File**: Select a previously uploaded Utilization File. This is the file that will be analyzed using the Matching Configuration. **Incumbent Network**: This is an optional field where you can select an Incumbent Network from the dropdown list. This list is populated with the client’s networks that have already been set up within Network360. Selecting an Incumbent Network will ignore ParStatus, if it was mapped. **Networks to Compare**: Select required networks from the dropdown list. This list is populated with the client’s networks and competitor networks available within Network360 when purchased by the client. If you do not see a desired network, please contact your account manager. **Matching Configuration**: Select the desired Matching Configuration to use in your analysis of the Utilization File. 3. Click the **Run Analysis** button. The Disruption Analyses list page will display. The name you gave to this analysis will be listed on the page with a Status of RUNNING. Once the analysis is complete, the Status will change to COMPLETED. **Note**: The larger the Utilization file and the more passes selected, the longer it will take to complete. ### Analysis Overview Once the status is COMPLETED on the Disruption Analyses List page, click on the Analysis Name in the first column. This will open the analysis. The **Show Analysis Criteria** link is present at the top left side of the Detailed Analysis Results page. If Show Analysis Criteria is clicked, it expands and displays the analysis criteria. Clicking on **Hide Analysis Criteria** collapses the details. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/disruption-detail-analysis-results-page-_show-analysis.png) The analysis criteria identifies the Name and Description of the analysis, along with the link to the Utilization File, Incumbent Network, Networks To Compare, and Matching Configuration that were used to generate the analysis. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/disruption-detailed-analysis-results-page_hide-analysis.png) Also, an **Edit Analysis Criteria** link will be displayed as shown in the above picture. Clicking on this link opens the Edit Analysis page. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/disruption_v2_editanalysis.png) There are 3 tabs on the **Detailed Analysis Results** page: Summary Overview, Providers, Manual Match. ### Summary Overview Tab There will be a column in the graph for each compare network that was selected. Radio buttons are available to select the view option (Confidence or INN/OO), and a link to the Utilization file is also provided. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/disruption-detail-analysis-results-page-_summary-overview.png) The graph columns will be color coded to show the confidence level of the matched provider data. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/summaryoverviewtab.png "SummaryOverviewTab") A color code key is provided in the right corner above the graph. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/summaryoverviewkey.png "SummaryOverviewKey") The **View** dropdown provides options to change the confidence levels included in the graph. The graph points out the number of providers in each confidence level and hovering the mouse over each section of the graph will display a pop-up with a brief explanation. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/matchedproviders.png "SummaryOverviewGraph") Below the graph is a list view of the same information. There are options to sort and filter the columns of the list view. Changing the sort or filtering will not change the graph. You can sort by a specific column by clicking the column header. You can change from ascending or descending by clicking the arrow. You can also find the **Sort by ASC** (ascending) and **Sort by DESC** (descending) options within the triple dot button along with the Filter and Column management options. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/filtersortmenu.png "FilterSortMenu") The **Filter** options allow for selecting a specific **Column**, the **Operator** (contains, equals, starts with, ends with, is empty, is not empty, is any of), and a **Value** field. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/filteroptions.png "FilterOptions") The **Hide Column** option will hide the selected column. The **Manage Columns** will open a pop-up box to select which columns to show/hide. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/columnsonoffsummary.png "ColumnsOnOffSummary") ### Providers Tab The Providers Tab contains a list of all the providers within the Utilization File. It is necessary to select a Network once on the Providers tab. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/providerstab-1.png "ProvidersTabNetworkSelected") Once a network is selected in the Providers tab, then the Provider List will display providers from the Utilization File that have been added, dropped, retained, or not available (not matched) and In-Network and Out-of-Network calculations. In-Network displays Provider status of Added, Retained, and Manual Match and Out-of-Network displays Provider status of Dropped, No Match. If the utilization file had duplicate entries of providers, it will merge them into a single record based on the Utilization File and Project Data using Matching Configuration. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/disruption-in-and-out-network-amounts.png "ProvidersTabList") * **Without an incumbent network selected**: The screenshot above shows the Providers tab with no incumbent network chosen. * **With an incumbent network selected**: The screenshot below shows the Providers tab with an incumbent network selected. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/disruption_v2_incumbentnetworks.png "WithIncumbent") The first 3 columns in the analysis will always be: * **Provider Name** **Provider Status** – Indicates if the provider is in the Incumbent Network and/or Compare Network(s). Each status is defined above the list.) Provider status is determined in the analysis using the below table:
| Incumbent Network Known | ParStatus Mapped | ParStatus Value | Matches Incumbent | Matches Evaluated | Status | | ----------------------- | ---------------- | --------------- | ----------------- | ----------------- | -------- | | No | Yes | Non-Par | N/A | Yes | Added | | No | Yes | Par | N/A | No | Dropped | | No | Yes | Unknown | N/A | Yes | Retained | | No | Yes | Unknown | No | Yes | N/A | | Yes | Ignored | Any | No | Yes | Added | | Yes | Ignored | Any | Yes | No | Dropped | | Yes | Ignored | Any | Yes | Yes | Retained | | Yes | Ignored | Any | No | No | N/A | | No | No | Any | N/A | Yes | Retained | | No | No | Any | N/A | No | N/A |
* **State(s) Served** – Indicates where the provider practices. Other provider fields available for selection include: * NPI * Tin Clicking on the ellipse’s menu in a column header and selecting **Manage Columns** allows you to add or remove columns using the toggle buttons. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/providerstabtoggle.png) The last 2 columns are dependent on business rules and what has been mapped in the Utilization File. * The data that can be displayed in the 2nd to last column, listed in priority order, are:\ Visits\ Claims\ Claimants\ Procedures\ \ If a Utilization File maps to more than one of these, it will display the higher priority data element. For example, if Visits and Claims were mapped, only Visits count will display. The priority business rules can be viewed by clicking on the “info i" next to the column header. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/infoiclaims.png "InfoIclaims") * The data that can be displayed in the last column, in priority order, are: \ Paid \ Billed \ Allowed \ \ If a Utilization File maps to more than one of these, it will display the higher priority data element. For example, if Paid and Billed were mapped, only Amount Paid will display. \ \ The priority business rules can be viewed by clicking on the “info i” next to the column header. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/paidbilledallowed.png "InfoIamountPaid") You can sort by a specific column by clicking the column header. You can change from ascending or descending by clicking the arrow. You can also find the **Sort by ASC** and **Sort by DESC** options within the triple dot button along with the Filter and Column management options. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/filtersortmenuoverview.png "FilterSortMenuOverview") The **Filter** options allow for selecting a specific **Column**, the **Operator** (contains, equals, starts with, ends with, is empty, is not empty, is any of), and a **Value** field. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/filteroptions.png "FilterOptions") The **Hide Column** option will hide the selected column. The **Manage Columns** will open a pop-up box to select which columns to show/hide. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/providerstabtoggle-2.png "ColumnsOnOff") ### Manual Match Tab Manual Match is available after a Disruption analysis has been run. This feature allows you to manually match the providers in the utilization file that did not match project data to the project data providers that are not matched. There are various reasons why providers would not be matched. For example, data errors in the utilization file (such as misspelled names, addresses, etc.) or the matching passes used. When you select the **Manual Match** tab, you will notice the **Network** field is pre-populated with the network from the **Providers** tab. This is purposely carried over to maintain continuity. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/manualmatchtab-1.png) The list of unmatched providers is displayed below the Network field. Note: These are the same providers that have a **Status** of **N/A** on the **Providers** tab. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/manualmatchtab-2.png "ManualMatchProviders") On this page you can: * Hide or Manage columns by selecting the triple dot button to the right of each column header. * Sort data columns up or down by clicking on the column header. * Select a listed provider to determine if a manual match should be made. \ Selecting **Match** in the **Action** column for a provider will bring you to Manual Match/Search for Providers page. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/manualmatch_searchproviders.png) The selected record is carried over and displays under **Manual Match**. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/manualmatchsinglerecord.png "ManualMatchSingleRecord") In the **Search for Providers** section, you can search by Name or NPI, Address, City, State, Zip, Tax ID or any combination of these fields. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/manualmatchsearch.png "ManualMatchSearch") Results will be displayed at the bottom of the page. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/mmresults.png "MMResults") Clicking on a provider name in the **Results** list will open the **Provider Details** page in a new tab. To research why a provider was not matched, you can download the **Analysis Detail CSV** and review the matching passes for the unmatched provider(s). If a provider result is determined to be a match, clicking **Match** in the **Actions** column will display a pop-up message to confirm linking the two providers together. You have the option to select Cancel or Match. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/mmconfirmation.png "MMConfirmation")
Selecting **Match** will update the **Summary Overview** and **Providers** tabs and returns you to the list of unmatched providers. Once a provider is matched you cannot undo the match with the provider. ### Analysis Reports The following Disruption reports are available for export in **Detail Analysis Results** page: #### Summary Overview tab ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/disruption_v2_summaryoverview-export.png) * Export Summary Overview (PDF) This report will export the Summary Overview graph and have benchmarks by selected network, along with aggregated counts by Confidence Match, No Match, and Manual Match. Open an Analysis from the Dashboard and then click on the Export Results button. * Export Detailed Analysis (CSV) This is a CSV export that contains all columns from the original utilization file, along with columns for each network match (yes or no), match confidence, matching pass that was used, and the internal Zelis Provider ID that the utilization row was matched to. There are two ways to download the full detail analysis csv: 1. Downloading from the Manage Analysis list, from the vertical ellipses. 2. From the Summary Overview tab in the analysis, under export. On the Analysis Dashboard page, click on the ellipses button (in the last column) and select Download. ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/analysisdetailsdownload.png)
#### Providers tab ![](/cms/cms-assets/media/disruption_v2_providers-export.png) * Top Providers (PDF) There are two types of Top 20 Providers export PDFs. * Export Top 20 Providers in Current Network * Export Top 20 Providers in All Networks These reports will provide the top 20 providers who were added, dropped, and retained by each network. Open an Analysis from the Dashboard, select the Providers tab, select a Network, and then click on the Export Results button. * Export All Providers (CSV) A CSV export of all providers for the selected network. Open an Analysis from the Dashboard, select the Providers tab, select a Network, and then click on the Export Results button. **Note:** This file will contain only the detail list of providers.
